title: Runtime Segmentation and Operator Tunnels Playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Purpose

This playbook defines a recommended pattern for runtime segmentation and short-lived operator tunnels for private (VPC and on-prem) Redwood deployments. It consolidates networking, security, and operational steps so field operators and SREs can safely perform day-0 installs, day-2 maintenance, and upgrades without widening long‑term network exposure.

Scope and audience
- Scope: Private deployments (VPC and on‑prem) where customers require operator access for troubleshooting, urgent rollbacks, or model swaps.
- Audience: Field operators, SREs, solution engineers, security reviewers, and customer infra teams.

Summary (one line)
Establish three runtime zones (Control, Tenant, Operator) and use ephemeral operator tunnels + policy gates to ensure operator tasks are auditable, rate-limited, and constrained by time and function.

Key definitions
- Control zone: Customer-managed control-plane components (API proxy, control services) that need minimal egress to Redwood telemetry endpoints.
- Tenant zone: Model serving runtime (GPU nodes, KV cache, local artifacts) that must be strongly isolated from operator networks.
- Operator zone: A narrow, purpose-built network / bastion cluster that enables temporary and logged connectivity for operator actions.
- Operator tunnel: An authenticated, timebound reverse/proxy tunnel (e.g., SSH reverse tunnel, mTLS-proxied channel) from customer network to Redwood operator tooling during a signed session.

Design goals and constraints
- Minimal blast radius: default deny between Tenant and Operator zones; explicit short-lived exceptions.
- Auditability: every operator session produces telemetry (session start, user, actions, command outputs) stored in customer-provided or Redwood-controlled append-only logs.
- Least privilege: operator access limited to specific ports, API endpoints, or kubectl verbs and only for listed service accounts.
- Network hygiene: small CIDR allocations, well-documented NAT/peering rules, no permanent inbound holes to Tenant nodes.
- Fail-safe rollback: operator tunnels must not be a dependency for automated rollback paths.

Reference topology (textual diagram)
Customer Network [VPC / On‑prem LAN]
  |
  +- Control zone (customer-managed subnets)
  |    - control-plane-proxy (tcp 8443), telemetry-forwarder (tcp 8888), kms-proxy
  |
  +- Tenant zone (isolated subnets or VLANs)
  |    - serving-nodes (gpus), kv-store, model-cache, s3-gateway
  |
  +- Operator zone (bastion / operator-proxy cluster)
       - ephemeral-bastion set (autoscaled), operator-proxy (mTLS), jump-proxy

Design pattern details
1) Zoning and CIDR guidance
- Tenant zone CIDR: /24 recommended for small installs (up to 50 nodes). Use /22 for larger clusters.
- Operator zone CIDR: single /28; keep small to minimize firewall rules.
- Control zone CIDR: separate /24.

2) Operator tunnel types (pick one per deployment)
- Reverse SSH (recommended for air-gapped + on‑prem): operator triggers a customer-hosted bootstrap that establishes a reverse SSH tunnel to Redwood's ephemeral operator pool. Reverse tunnel only exposes port ranges required for the task. Example: ssh -R 22000:localhost:8443 operator@ephemeral-ops.redwood.example --key-file ~/.ssh/ops_key -o "ExitOnForwardFailure=yes" -N
- mTLS-proxied HTTP (recommended for VPC): customer proxy component (control-plane-proxy) establishes outbound mTLS to Redwood operator-proxy; operator sessions are multiplexed over authenticated HTTP/2 streams and gated by signed SVIDs.
- Service mesh sidecar (optional): when a mesh is present, use a control-plane-managed sidecar that only accepts operator commands over a mTLS-validated endpoint.

3) Authentication and session gating
- All operator sessions MUST be tied to ephemeral service accounts and short-lived credentials (max TTL 1h).
- Multi-factor sign-off required for destructive actions (model-swap, tenant-eviction). MFA can be delegated to customer IdP (SAML/OIDC) or Redwood's enterprise auth bridge.
- Actions must be recorded in tamper-evident logs and linked to a change ticket ID (format: RDW-TKT-<YYYYMMDD>-<seq>).

Network and firewall matrix (apply at ACLs/firewalls/load balancers)
| Source | Destination | Ports | Purpose | TTL for rule |
|--------|-------------|-------|---------|---------------|
| Operator zone | control-plane-proxy | tcp 8443 | management API, RPC | 1 hour (ephemeral)
| Operator zone | telemetry-forwarder | tcp 8888 | log/trace retrieval | 1 hour
| Control zone | Tenant zone | tcp 443, tcp 10250 | model-control endpoints, kubelet (read-only) | permanent (narrowed by SA)
| Tenant zone | External S3 | tcp 443 | model artifact fetch | permanent (TLS)
| External Redwood Operator IPs | Operator zone | tcp 22 / tcp 443 | operator bootstrap (reverse connections) | permanent for bootstrap origin set (customer-managed)

Operational playbook (step-by-step)
1) Preflight (customer & Redwood)
   a) Confirm CIDRs: customer provides tenant/control/operator CIDRs and BGP/peering diagram.
   b) Validate KMS/HSM reachability from control-plane-proxy.
   c) Provision operator service accounts in customer IdP with TTL 1h.
   d) Run smoke tests: control-proxy -> control-api (GET /health), kubelet read-only probe.

2) Establish ephemeral operator tunnel (example, reverse SSH flow)
   1. Customer runs bootstrap script (provided as redwood-bootstrap.sh) which:
      - generates ephemeral key pair,
      - starts local agent and registers session with control-plane-proxy,
      - establishes reverse SSH tunnel: ssh -R <remote-port>:localhost:<local-mgmt-port> operator@ops-gateway.redwood.internal -i /tmp/ephemeral_key -N
   2. Operator requests session via Redwood Operator Console: selects customer, supplies ticket ID, and triggers the session.
   3. Customer operator-agent validates session and opens proxied connection to target service.

3) Common operator tasks and safe commands
- Non-destructive: read logs, gather telemetry, run read-only diagnostic kubectl commands: kubectl get pods --namespace model-runtime -o wide
- Destructive (requires MFA & change ticket): model-swap, rolling restart of serving nodes, tenant eviction. Operators must follow the destructive action checklist.

4) Closing session and artifact retention
- Operator terminates session via console. Customer agent tears down reverse tunnels and rotates ephemeral keys.
- Telemetry and audit bundle (JSON) is pushed to customer log sink and to Redwood evidence storage if customer permits retention.

Upgrade and rollback guidance (safe path)
- Canary first: route 10% of traffic to new runtime image + new quantization profile for 24h. Observe p50/p95 latency and error rate.
- If latency p95 > baseline * 1.2 OR error rate increases > 0.5% absolute, trigger immediate rollback.
- Rollback steps (operator tunnel required only for emergency manual rollback):
  1. Mark canary as draining in control-plane.
  2. Trigger model-artifact revert: apply previous model config through control API (POST /v1/models/activate with model_id).
  3. Gracefully drain nodes (kubectl cordon/drain) and re-provision from previous image.
  4. Validate serving correctness against golden prompt set (see "acceptance tests" below).

Safety checks and guardrails (automated)
- Auto-rollforward prevention: if telemetry ingestion or control-plane reconcilers detect >5% unknown-state pods during upgrade, pause rollout.
- Operator kill-switch: an automated runbook that toggles a global 'quarantine' flag prevents operator-initiated destructive calls until manual review.

Acceptance tests and examples
- Golden prompt set: run 25 synthetic prompts that exercise long-context KV-cache behavior; expected BLEU-like/semantic match score above 0.82 vs baseline.
- Latency test: 1k synthetic requests at target QPS; p95 latency <= 1.2x production baseline.
- Example health-check curl: curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://control-proxy.internal:8443/health | jq

YAML snippet: ephemeral operator session registration
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: operator-session-config
  namespace: operator-proxy
data:
  session_ttl: "3600"
  allowed_ports: "8443,8888"
---

Roles and ownership
- Field Operator (Redwood): session initiation, guidance for destructive actions (on-call duty).
- Customer Platform Owner: firewall rule authoring, KMS/HSM oversight, final permission grant.
- SRE Owner (Redwood): automation of canary analysis and rollback triggers.
- Security Reviewer: periodic audit of operator access logs and ticket correlation.

Checklist: customer requirements before enabling operator tunnels
| Item | Required | Notes |
|------|----------|-------|
| CIDR allocation for operator zone | Yes | /28 recommended |
| Customer IdP integration | Yes | SAML/OIDC with short TTL tokens |
| KMS/HSM endpoint reachable from control zone | Yes | TLS mutual auth recommended |
| Logging sink (S3/ELK) configured | Yes | must accept signed audit bundles |
| Change ticketing system API | Optional but recommended | Redwood can integrate for ticket correlation |

Testing catalog (must pass before Golive)
- Connectivity: verify operator session lifecycle (establish, operate, teardown) three times.
- Security: run penetration checklist 10 items (bastion hardening, keys rotation, ACL verification).
- Functional: golden prompts for model correctness and token accounting checks.

Incident runbook (operator tunnel related)
1) Symptom: operator session cannot establish (timeout on reverse SSH).
   - Check 1: confirm bootstrap agent is running on customer host.
   - Check 2: verify egress rules for outbound to ops-gateway.redwood.internal:22/443.
   - Quick fix: have customer restart bootstrap agent; if still failing, escalate to Network SRE.
2) Symptom: unauthorized operator action detected.
   - Immediate: revoke ephemeral SA, rotate agent key, and set quarantine flag.
   - Postmortem: correlate ticket ID -> session logs -> commands; report to security.

Operational metrics to monitor
- Operator session success rate (target 99.5% per month).
- Average session duration (goal < 25 minutes for diagnostics).
- Number of destructive actions / month (goal: keep < 3; requires change ticket).
- Audit bundle delivery latency (goal < 5 minutes).

Appendix A: Example bootstrap script outline (redwood-bootstrap.sh)
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
TMP_KEY=$(mktemp /tmp/ops_key.XXXX)
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ${TMP_KEY} -N ''
# Register ephemeral key with control-proxy
curl -X POST https://control-proxy.internal:8443/api/v1/operator/register -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"pubkey":"'"$(cat ${TMP_KEY}.pub)"'","ticket":"$1"}'
# Start reverse SSH (blocking)
ssh -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes -i ${TMP_KEY} -R 22000:localhost:8443 operator@ops-gateway.redwood.internal -N
